entries.claim: The format-1 fixture is stamped with the current `DERIVED_SCHEMA`, so the test does not exercise opening a real older store whose archive and derived-schema versions are both old.
entries.failure_scenario: If store opening checks or rebuilds a mismatched derived schema before rejecting the archive format, an actual format-1 store can execute the CREATE TABLE/INDEX migration and then fail as half-upgraded. Every case in this test still passes because the fixture's derived schema already equals the current binary's version, bypassing the write-producing migration path.

counter_evidence.note: The scenario needs a derived-schema check or rebuild ahead of the archive refusal, and there is none. read_versions refuses an older archive format at open.rs:754 before the derived-schema comparison at :762, and both opens call it on a SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY connection (open.rs:248-268 and :696-704), which cannot run CREATE TABLE. The fixture is also what a real format-1 store carries: DERIVED_SCHEMA has been 4 since ea1b181 (2026-10-05), the binary that wrote the owner store, and this phase did not change it.

entries.claim: The asserted every-command coverage explicitly omits `mcp`, even though its different response protocol does not prevent testing refusal and byte preservation.
entries.failure_scenario: If MCP startup opens a format-1 store through a path that migrates or writes before returning its protocol-level error, this test remains green. The test can start MCP, send a request or initialization transcript, assert the refusal reason, terminate it, and compare the database and WAL bytes just as it does for exit-based commands.

counter_evidence.note: MCP has no separate open path to migrate through. It opens the store per call, read-only, through cmd::read::open (mcp/mod.rs:22-25), which is Store::open_read_only (cmd/read.rs:96-97), the same read-only open the test already drives through the CLI read commands; a READ_ONLY connection cannot write before the refusal.
